analysis.title: TC Energy Corp. (TRP.TO): Key Takeaways from NDR: Canada Growth Opportunity Accelerating, Complementing US Gas Growth - Buy
key_insights: GS hosted TC Energy (TRP/TRP.TO, Buy) for an NDR to Chicago and Dallas on 11/18-19/26 with CFO Sean O'Donnell and David Brast, President US Gas Pipelines. GS reiterates Buy after what it calls a material turnaround in the TRP story over three years.

TRP disclosed a new C$15b Canada power opportunity in its projects-in-origination backlog with 3Q26 earnings. It is a bottom-up, unrisked list of potential projects, and the company has worked on it since last summer. The focus is Canada only, across multiple provinces, where TRP can use its incumbent gas pipeline, land, community and government relations position.

Data centers are the core focus of the Canada power effort. TRP targets initial proof-of-concept deals of about 300 MW, 1-2 of them by the 4Q26 earnings release, then larger deployments. TRP would own and operate the power and gas pipeline laterals and offer hyperscalers a land and power package anchored by a take-or-pay PPA.

TRP expects premium pricing of about 3-4x Alberta spot under Bill C-39, which GS believes could allow low-teens returns. Construction could take 2-3 years and allow 3+ GW over multiple sites. TRP plans to partner with OEMs (about 3 technologies across recips, turbines and fuel cells, plus batteries) and possibly a data center developer. Federal support is the key swing factor for whether the effort falls short of or exceeds C$15b.

TRP is working on a negotiated settlement on NGTL, the 'new investment framework', on top of the current cost-of-service structure. All 300+ customers would need to agree. Customer interest over the summer implied C$6b of capital over 5 years to C$20b over 10 years. TRP is pushing for higher returns than the current NGTL structure gives.

The Alberta Growth Connector could move forward at C$3-4b, with targeted returns 100-200bps above the current NGTL structure and in-service later this decade, if negotiations conclude near-term (1H27). GS says failure would modestly disappoint medium-term growth but could drive a restructuring of the regulated framework when the NGTL rate settlement expires in 2029+.

US gas sanctioning rose from about US$1b/year historically to about US$2b in 2025 and about US$4b in 2026, with a goal of a higher level in 2027. Interconnect requests on TRP's US gas pipeline systems reached about 190 through 3Q26, versus 140 in 2025 and 85 in 2024. Management cites coal-to-gas switching as a secular driver, with 26 coal plants near its assets set to retire by 2030.

TRP sanctioned the US$1.8b Crossroads expansion in the Midwest at a 6.0x build multiple. It adds about 1.4 bcf/d for a 2030 in-service, backed by 20-year take-or-pay contracts. Capital came in above GS's prior expectation of north of US$1.4b because scope was upsized after an open season that was 2.5x oversubscribed. Crossroads could add another 0.7-1.0 bcf/d with compression. ASP was upsized to a 48-inch line.

TRP's backlog is C$30b (24/6 split between sanctioned and pending approval) plus a C$40b origination set. It extended its 5-7% comparable EBITDA CAGR guidance to 2026-2031. The 5% low end is effectively reached with the existing backlog. The midpoint needs C$6b of origination projects and the high end C$12b, which would lift annual spend from C$6b to C$8b or C$10b, mostly in 2029-31. GS sees the high end as increasingly likely.
The new guidance range implies about C$15.92b of 2031 EBITDA at the midpoint off the 2026 guide, versus GS's estimate of C$15.51b.

Management called 4.75x leverage (on its calculation) an inviolable ceiling and said equity issuance is off the table. Funding levers for upside growth are base business outperformance (AI-driven cost savings in US gas pipelines, with Columbia next in 2027), asset sales (about 6 candidates, with the Mexico asset sale as an example), and private credit bridging of C$2-3b for 3-4 years across 2029-31.

Repayment of the 2029-31 bridge relies on Bruce Power, where the MCR program wraps early next decade and returns C$2-3b of ramping cash flow to TRP. GS sees this flexibility holding even if TRP proceeds with Bruce C.

Bruce C (up to about 4.8 GW) is in early pre-development, with about C$300m of government funding secured. Hypothetical cost is about C$60b gross, needing about C$20b of equity, half of it TRP's share, or roughly C$1b/year over about 10 years. GS expects FID around 2030, early 2030s at the earliest for a decision, and late 2029 at the earliest.

GS rates TRP.TO Buy with a C$102 12-month price target and TRP Buy with a US$73 target, based on 14.75x 2027 EBITDA. Price at the 19 Nov 2026 close was C$90.11 (13.2% upside) and US$62.81 (16.2% upside). The targets were unchanged from 13-Nov-26.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after the NDR, citing Canada power, NGTL and US gas growth, and a likely high-end 5-7% EBITDA CAGR to 2031. The target uses 14.75x 2027 EBITDA.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 update (reported, per the report): TRP sanctioned the US$1.8b Crossroads expansion, updated its sanctioned and pending-approval backlog to C$30b, announced a C$40b origination set, and extended the 5-7% comparable EBITDA CAGR guidance to 2026-2031.

GS forecasts (estimates, not reported): EBITDA C$12,015.7mn for 12/26E, C$12,392.9mn for 12/27E and C$13,030.1mn for 12/28E, versus C$10,952.0mn in 12/25. EPS is C$3.84 for 12/26E, C$4.03 for 12/27E and C$4.26 for 12/28E, versus C$3.51 in 12/25.
GS quarterly EPS estimates are C$0.96 for 12/26E, C$1.09 for 3/27E and C$0.93 for 6/27E. EPS for 9/26 is C$0.94.
Management expects the new guidance range to imply about C$15.92b of 2031 EBITDA at the midpoint of the 2026 guide, versus GS's estimate of C$15.51b.
risk_factors: Softer than expected execution on gas and/or power projects.
Higher regulatory hurdles for natural gas pipeline and nuclear projects.
Higher than expected capex requirements and lower return profiles on FID'd projects.
Counterparty concentration risks on Mexico transmission assets.
NGTL settlement talks could fail, since all 300+ customers must agree.
Federal support for Canada power projects could disappoint.
geopolitical: Canada's relative appeal versus the US after the elections, which management stressed did not change projects already in flight.
Federal support in Canada and Bill C-39 are described as key to the power opportunity.
US permitting reform is seen as increasingly likely but is not in TRP's outlook or timelines.

tension_points.bull_case: A new investment framework could lift NGTL growth, and the Alberta Growth Connector could proceed at C$3-4b with returns 100-200bps above the current structure.
tension_points.bear_case: All 300+ customers must agree, and a failed process would be modestly disappointing for medium-term growth. GS sees longer-term upside for 2029+ from a possible restructuring of the regulated structure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Negotiations not completed near-term (1H27) for the Alberta Growth Connector.

tension_points.bull_case: C$15b of bottom-up projects, 3+ GW over multiple sites, premium pricing of 3-4x Alberta spot and low-teens returns, with 1-2 initial deals targeted by the 4Q26 earnings release.
tension_points.bear_case: Federal support remains the key focus and could determine whether the effort disappoints or exceeds C$15b.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No initial proof-of-concept deals by the 4Q26 earnings release, or weak federal support.

theme_stances.key_argument: TRP's incumbent gas pipeline position and speed-to-market under Bill C-39 support premium pricing and low-teens returns.
theme_stances.evidence: the Canada power opportunity is material, with potential near-term catalysts

theme_stances.key_argument: The C$30b backlog already reaches the 5% low end, and power, NGTL and US gas wins could fill the wedge to the high end.
theme_stances.evidence: the high-end of the recently guided 5-7% EBITDA CAGR to 2031 appearing increasingly likely
